epic.intent:
Plan in Dark Mechanicus, work in Linear. A person authorizes the transfer of a saved DM epic. An orchestrator agent then carries it out once, through its own connection to Linear's hosted MCP server, into a Linear project:

- **DM epic → Linear project.** The name is the epic title. The summary (255 characters at most) is the back-link and the item's marker. The content is the intent and the success criteria.
- **DM sprint → project milestone**, in sprint order ("Sprint N: goal").
- **DM ticket → issue** in its sprint's milestone, created in execution order: sprint, then dependency row, then the sprint's own order. Identifiers therefore rise in execution order, and the manual sort order matches when Linear's MCP lets it be set.
- **Each sprint's acceptance node → the last issue of its milestone**, blocked by every required work issue of that sprint.
- **Links:** dependency edges → "blocks" relations; `related_to` → "related"; `duplicate_of` is named in the description.
- **Fields:**
  - acceptance criteria → a Markdown checklist in the description;
  - priority → Linear priority (critical Urgent, high High, normal Medium, low Low);
  - tags → labels (an existing label of the same name is reused, otherwise one is created);
  - the DM key, epic id, references and a `dm:<epicId>/<ref>` marker stay in the description;
  - no estimates.
- **State:** DM tickets already completed → a completed-type Linear state; the rest → the team's default state.

The transfer is a one-time handoff: Linear becomes the board.
- **Recording and resume:** DM records each DM → Linear id as the agent creates it. Before creating anything, the agent searches Linear for the item's marker. An interrupted transfer therefore resumes without duplicates, even after a crash between a create and its record.
- **Verification:** when everything is created, the agent reads the project back through Linear's MCP and submits that read-back. DM compares it with the stored transfer packet. Only an exact match completes the DM epic. The transfer record holds the Linear project URL and every DM key → Linear identifier.
- **Locking:** while a transfer is open, the epic cannot be run or its plan saved. The person can cancel the transfer. A completed epic is read-only, so it can be neither run nor transferred again.

**Authorization and start.** An agent can never start a transfer on its own: the person authorizes each one in the desktop app, as queuing a run works today. There are two ways to start:
- **Transfer to Linear** in the epic workspace authorizes the transfer and starts an orchestrator agent in an in-app chat.
- **Copy prompt** in the same dialog (or `dm transfer linear --epic <id>` once the transfer is authorized) gives the same prompt to an agent started elsewhere.

**Linear connection.** The agent uses the Linear MCP server configured in its own CLI. The dialog and the prompt give the exact setup commands, and the person completes Linear's browser sign-in and picks the team in the chat.

Linear only: no tracker abstraction, and Jira is a later epic.

**Planning change first.** The epic starts with a DM-wide planning change, at the owner's request: standards beyond a project's Definition of Done apply to an epic only when its planner states them in the plan. That covers tests written first, test-quality grading such as Fireguard, and per-sprint grading tickets. Every ticket lists its tests, and its worker writes and runs them in that ticket.

### Standards for this epic (planner statement)

- Each work ticket's **Tests** section lists the tests to write. The worker writes and runs them in that ticket, in any order; tests-first is not required.
- No Fireguard ticket or run inside this epic. CI still grades the merge PR. The acceptance node runs the project's Definition of Done once, on the combined work; Fireguard is out of that Definition of Done before the run starts (entry criterion n2).
- Work tickets run only their targeted checks: typecheck, lint on touched files, the listed tests and the existing tests of touched files.

successCriteria.text: A saved epic becomes a Linear project with one milestone per sprint in sprint order and one issue per ticket created in execution order. Each acceptance node is last in its milestone, dependencies are blocks relations, and every issue carries the criteria checklist, priority, labels, DM back-link and marker.

DM completes the epic only after the submitted read-back matches the stored packet. Any mismatch keeps the transfer open and names each difference by DM key and field, including extra or duplicate items in Linear.
An interrupted transfer resumes from the recorded mapping and the markers, and creates nothing twice.

A verified transfer leaves the epic completed with a transfer record (Linear project URL, revision, and every DM key → Linear identifier). The epic then refuses runs, plan edits and further transfers.

Only a person can authorize a transfer, from the desktop app. It then runs in an in-app orchestrator chat or in an agent started elsewhere with the copied prompt or `dm transfer linear`, and runs and plan saves are refused until it is verified or canceled.
Planning defaults: the role guides and this repository's rules apply tests-first and Fireguard only when a plan states them, and every ticket lists the tests its worker writes.

epic.title: Linear handoff: transfer a saved plan to a Linear project in execution order, verify it, and complete the epic

bundle.rationale:
## Decisions

The owner set these on 2026-10-30:
- **One-time handoff, not sync.** Transfer, verify, then complete the DM epic. There is no re-export, no status pull-back and no two-way sync. Linear becomes the board.
- **The orchestrator agent writes to Linear** through Linear's hosted MCP server (`https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`, OAuth in the browser), with the person's help to sign in. DM holds no Linear credential. DM's part is deterministic: the stored, ordered packet, the id mapping, the read-back comparison and the completion.
- **Order:** creation order, manual sort order, "blocks" relations and clean titles.
- **Fields:** criteria checklist, priority, labels, the DM key and back-link. No estimates.
- **Acceptance node** → the last issue of its milestone.
- **Partial transfers** resume and get fixed; nothing in Linear is deleted.
- **Completion** → the epic is completed, with a transfer record.
- **Linear only**, with no tracker abstraction.
- **Standards:** the DM-wide default change lands first, in this epic. One sprint. Tests are listed and written in each ticket. No Fireguard.

The planner added these after review:
- **A person authorizes each transfer.** This is a human-only `transfer.queue`, mirroring `run.queue`. Without it, any orchestrator session could submit a read-back and permanently complete an epic. After authorization, completion on an exact match needs no second approval.
- **The agent's own Linear connection.** The in-app adapters deliberately attach no extra MCP server, because managed policies refuse dynamically configured ones. In-app chats already load the person's own servers, so DM supplies the setup commands rather than a bundled bridge.
- **Identifier order is a warning, not a mismatch.** It cannot be repaired without deleting issues. All identifiers must share one team key.
- **The mapping lives in `outcome.transfer.items`.** A comment is capped at 20,000 characters, and an epic can hold 1,000 tickets.

## Shape

One sprint. Row 1 lands the standards change (role guides and repository rules) next to the pure packet builder. The core then runs in order:
1. the progress store with authorization and cancel;
2. verification and completion, alongside the run and save locks;
3. the commands and tools;
4. the guide, the kickoff and the CLI;
5. the fake-Linear end-to-end test, alongside the in-app chat start;
6. the workspace UI;
7. the docs.

The acceptance node runs the project's Definition of Done once.

## Risks

- **Verification trusts the agent's read-back.** DM cannot read Linear itself. The read-back carries Linear's own ids. DM checks it structurally against the stored packet and the recorded mapping, covering text, membership, extras, duplicates and relations. It cannot prove that the agent did not invent a read-back. The human authorization bounds who can try.
- **Linear MCP coverage is unverified here** (no sandbox workspace; mock only). The guide discovers tool names at run time. Sort order and identifier order are warnings.
- **Fireguard leaves the project Definition of Done before the run** (entry criterion n2). That needs a planner `set_definition_of_done` plus the matching `src/core/repo/repoProject.test.ts` update, committed together on main.

acceptanceCriteria.text: buildLinearPacket orders issues by sprint ordinal, then planRows row, then the sprint's ticket order, with each acceptance node last in its milestone.
Relations hold every dependency edge, each acceptance node blocked by its sprint's required work tickets, and related_to as related, with no duplicates.

Issues carry the Linear priority number, tags as labels, the completed state for completed tickets, and a description with the criteria checklist, the DM key back-link and the marker as its last line. The project summary is at most 255 characters.
packetHash is deterministic and changes with content.
The listed tests in linearPacket.test.ts pass.

tickets.body:
**Change**
Add the pure function `buildLinearPacket(input)` in `src/core/transfer/linearPacket.ts` (no I/O). Its input is the epic, a saved `PlanBundle`, the revision id and number, and the ticket statuses. Its output is a `LinearTransferPacket`, with the types in `src/shared/domain/transfer.ts`.

The packet is `{ format: 'darkmechanicus.linear-transfer', version: 1, epicId, revisionId, packetHash, project, milestones, issues, relations }`.
- **marker:** every project, milestone and issue carries `marker: 'dm:<epicId>/<ref>'`. It is written as the last line of the item's text, and the agent searches for it before creating.
- **project:** `{ ref: 'project', marker, name, summary, content }`.
  - `name`: the epic title.
  - `summary`: 255 characters at most, "From Dark Mechanicus: epic <id>, revision <n>" followed by the marker.
  - `content`: the intent and the success criteria.
- **milestones:** one per sprint by `ordinal`: `{ ref: sprintId, marker, position, name: 'Sprint N: <first line of goal>', description }`. The description holds the goal, the exit criteria and the marker.
- **issues**, in execution order: by `sortedSprints`, then `planRows` row, then the sprint's `ticketIds` order, with the acceptance node last in its milestone. Each is `{ ref: ticketId, key, marker, position (1-based across the epic), milestoneRef, title, description, priority, labels, state, blockedBy }`:
  - `priority`: Linear's numbers (critical 1, high 2, normal 3, low 4).
  - `labels`: the tags.
  - `state`: 'completed' for a completed ticket, 'default' otherwise.
  - `description`, in order:
    - the body;
    - "Acceptance criteria" as a `- [ ] c1 …` checklist (an acceptance node's items name the covered key);
    - the references, and any `duplicate_of`;
    - "DM key DM-123 · epic <id> · revision <n>";
    - the marker.
    Optional tickets say so.
- **relations:** `{ ref: 'rel:<blockerId>:<blockedId>', kind: 'blocks', blockerRef, blockedRef }` (the ref fits the 64-character `entityRef` limit).
  - There is one per dependency edge.
  - Each acceptance node is also blocked by `implicitPrerequisitesOf` (`src/core/plan/acceptance.ts`).
  - Each `related_to` gives a `kind: 'related'` relation.
  - Deduplicated, in issue order.
- **packetHash:** the `contentHash` of the canonical packet, computed without the hash itself.

**Tests** (write and run in this ticket), in `src/core/transfer/linearPacket.test.ts`:
- Execution order across two sprints, with three rows and an in-row order that differs from the ids. The acceptance node comes last and is blocked by exactly its sprint's required (non-optional) work tickets.
- Relations:
  - edges become blocks relations in the right direction;
  - an explicit edge that repeats an acceptance prerequisite adds no duplicate;
  - `related_to` becomes related;
  - a `duplicate_of` appears in the description.
- Fields: each priority maps to its number; tags become labels; a completed ticket gets state 'completed'.
- Text: the issue description ends with the back-link and the marker; the project summary is at most 255 characters; milestone names follow "Sprint N: …".
- The hash is stable for the same input and changes when a title changes.

**Checks:** typecheck; `npx oxlint` on the files you touched; the tests listed above plus the existing tests of the files you touched. Do not run the full suite, coverage, whole-tree lint, a build (unless a criterion needs one) or Fireguard.

tickets.body:
**Change**
- Add `skills/linear-transfer.md`. Its first line is the description and its body starts with `# Linear transfer`. It is the guide the orchestrator follows:
  1. Call `get_capabilities` and confirm the role is orchestrator. Then call `start_transfer`. If it says the person has not authorized the transfer, stop and ask them to press Transfer to Linear in the app.
  2. Check that Linear's MCP tools are available.
     - If they are not, stop and give the person the setup for your CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http linear-server https://mcp.linear.app/mcp` then `/mcp` to sign in; `codex mcp add linear --url https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`; Cursor's MCP settings. Wait until they are done.
     - If a sign-in is pending, ask the person to complete it in the browser.
  3. List the teams and ask the person which team to use.
  4. Find each label or create it, reusing one of the same name.
  5. Create the project, then the milestones in position order, then the issues strictly in `position` order, one at a time.
     - Before each create, search Linear for the item's `marker`. If you find it, record that item instead of creating a new one.
     - Call `record_transfer_item` right after each creation.
  6. Set the completed state where the packet says so.
     - Add the relations, after listing the blocked issue's existing relations so none is added twice.
     - Set the sort order when a tool allows it.
  7. Read the project back and call `submit_transfer_readback`. Send it in parts when it is large, with `final: true` on the last. A submission may ask the person for approval.
     - Fix each mismatch by updating the Linear item, or by moving an unexpected one out of the project; never delete.
     - Then submit again.
  8. After an interruption, continue from `get_transfer` `next`. Never complete the epic any other way.
- Register it in `SKILLS` (`src/mcp/skills.ts`). That serves it as the `darkmechanicus-linear-transfer` prompt and installs it through `skillInstall`.
  - Update `EXPECTED` in `src/mcp/skills.test.ts` and the prompt count in `src/mcp/server.test.ts`.
  - Add the Linear words to `VOCABULARY` where needed.
  - Do not bump `SKILLS_VERSION` again.
- Add `transferKickoff(input)` and `transferTitle` ("Linear transfer · <epic>"), mirroring `orchestratorKickoff`. Put them in a module the main process and the CLI bundle can both import.
  - The kickoff holds the epic title (one line, masked), the epic id, the steps, and the guide text from `skillBody('linear-transfer')`.
  - The in-app chat, Copy prompt and the CLI all print this same text.
- CLI `dm transfer linear --epic <id> [--json]`:
  - Add a `{ kind: 'transfer', target: 'linear', epicId, json }` mode to `modeOf` in `src/cli/args.ts`, `--epic` to `VALUE_FLAGS`, and `--json` as a switch for this mode only. Update `CLI_USAGE`.
  - Output: the kickoff and a summary of the packet (counts per milestone, the first issues in order), the Linear setup lines, and how to give the agent an orchestrator grant (the Agent access card, `DM_SESSION_TOKEN`). When the transfer is not authorized yet, it says so first.
  - `--json` prints the packet.
  - It is read-only, works for a reader, and is the only mode that prints text instead of the JSON envelope; say so in `docs/runbooks/cli.md`.

**Tests** (write and run in this ticket):
- Update the skill and prompt tests: names, count, vocabulary.
- The kickoff test: it names the epic id, includes the guide body, masks a claim-token-like title, and the title is cut to `LIMITS.title`.
- `src/cli/args.test.ts` and `src/cli/main.test.ts`:
  - `transfer linear` rejects a missing `--epic`;
  - it prints the kickoff for a known epic, as a reader;

acceptanceCriteria.text: Importing a saved revision for an epic with a queued or in-progress transfer reports a storage conflict naming the epic, and leaves the local revision and transfer unchanged.

After cancelTransfer, reconciling imports the revision and the run.

tickets.body:
**Context**
`src/core/repo/importer.ts` inserts saved `plan_revisions` and `runs` from portable state without `assertNoOpenTransfer` (`src/core/services/transferGuard.ts`), and the `transfers` table is local only. Another machine can save a plan or start a run while a transfer is open here, and a pull imports it, leaving a run and an open transfer on one epic (found in DM-289).

**Change**
- When an import would add a saved revision newer than the open transfer's `revision_id`, or a run, for an epic whose local transfer is `queued` or `in_progress`, do not apply it silently. Report a storage conflict for that epic through the existing conflict path that `get_storage_status` and `reconcile_repository` already use, naming the epic and the open transfer, and leave the local revision, run and transfer unchanged.
- The person resolves it by canceling the transfer and reconciling again. Imports for epics with no transfer, or a canceled or verified one, behave as before.
- Do not make transfers portable in this ticket.

**Tests** (write and run in this ticket)
- `src/core/repo/importer.test.ts`: an incoming saved revision while a transfer is queued, and while it is in progress, is reported as a conflict and not applied; an incoming run likewise; after `cancelTransfer`, reconciling imports both.

tickets.body:
**Context**
`linearReadback` (`src/core/schemas.ts`) bounds each field and list, but one part can still be hundreds of MB (1,000 issues x 500,000-character descriptions), and `acceptReadbackPart` (`src/core/services/transfers.ts`) merges any number of non-final parts into `transfers.readback_json` without a cap (found in DM-291).

**Change**
- Cap the serialized size of one `readback` part at the command boundary (the `submitTransferReadback` command schema or handler), and refuse a larger part with `invalid_input` before it is merged.
- Cap the merged totals in `acceptReadbackPart`: milestones, issues and relations each at most their packet-side limit plus a fixed allowance for unexpected items. A part that would exceed a cap is refused with `invalid_input` naming the limit, and the stored parts stay as they were.
- Keep `submitTransferReadback` outside any outer transaction (its runtime guard stays).
- Name the limits as constants next to `LIMITS` and state them in `docs/runbooks/linear-transfer.md`.

- Non-final parts whose merged issues exceed the cap are refused, and the earlier parts remain.
